question: Which of the following is a feature of the State Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) in India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: It can be dissolved like the Legislative Assembly
The people directly elect their members
It has a fixed term of five years
It is a permanent body and cannot be dissolved
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is It is a permanent body and cannot be dissolved

Explanation:
The State Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) in India is an upper house that is a permanent body. It cannot be dissolved; instead, one-third of its members retire every two years. Members of the Legislative Council are elected indirectly through members of the Legislative Assembly, local bodies, teachers, and graduates. It does not have a fixed term; it continues permanently. Unlike the Legislative Assembly, it cannot be dissolved. Currently, only 6 states have a Legislative Council.

☛ Election of members → Indirect election
☛ Term of one-third members → Retire every two years
☛ Number of states with Legislative Council → 6
☛ Creation of Legislative Council → Under Article 169 of the Constitution

question: Which of the following is NOT a Central Armed Police Force?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 3)

question: Who is responsible for the administration of Union Territories like Chandigarh and Lakshadweep?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: The President of India
Prime Minister of India directly
Elected Chief Ministers of the Union Territories
Governors of neighbouring states
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The President of India

Explanation:
According to Article 239 of the Indian Constitution, the administration of every Union Territory is carried out by the President of India. The President exercises these powers through an Administrator or Lieutenant Governor. Chandigarh is administered directly by the Central Government, while Lakshadweep is administered by an Administrator. Except for Delhi and Puducherry, no Union Territory has an elected Chief Minister. The President can also issue ordinances to make rules for the administration of Union Territories. This provision is covered under Part VIII of the Constitution.

☛ Which Article deals with administration of Union Territories? → Article 239
☛ Which Union Territories have Chief Ministers? → Delhi and Puducherry

☛ Who administers Lakshadweep? → Administrator
question_hi: चंडीगढ़ और लक्षद्वीप जैसे केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों के प्रशासन के लिए कौन जिम्मेदार है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (28/08/2025) Shift 3)

केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों के निर्वाचित मुख्यमंत्री

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है भारत के राष्ट्रपति

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 239 के अनुसार, प्रत्येक केंद्र शासित प्रदेश का प्रशासन राष्ट्रपति द्वारा किया जाता है। राष्ट्रपति अपनी शक्तियों का प्रयोग प्रशासक या उपराज्यपाल के माध्यम से करता है। चंडीगढ़ का प्रशासन सीधे केंद्र सरकार द्वारा चलाया जाता है, जबकि लक्षद्वीप का प्रशासन एक प्रशासक द्वारा किया जाता है। पुदुचेरी और दिल्ली को छोड़कर, सभी केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों में कोई निर्वाचित मुख्यमंत्री नहीं होता। राष्ट्रपति केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों के प्रशासन के लिए नियम बनाने हेतु अध्यादेश जारी कर सकते हैं। यह प्रावधान संविधान के भाग VIII में दिया गया है।

question: Which of the following States enjoys special provisions under Article 371A due to its unique customary law and land ownership practices? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (29/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Sikkim
Mizoram
Nagaland
Manipur
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Nagaland

Explanation:
Article 371A provides special provisions to the state of Nagaland. This article was added in 1963 when Nagaland was granted statehood. Its main purpose is to protect the customary law, land ownership, and socio-religious practices of the Naga people. Under this provision, laws passed by Parliament will apply to Nagaland only if the state's legislature adopts them. This ensures the preservation of Nagaland's unique cultural identity and traditional governance system. Similar special provisions exist for other northeastern states like Mizoram (Article 371G) and Assam (Article 371B), but Nagaland enjoys the most autonomy under Article 371A.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which state is related to Article 371A? → Nagaland
☛ When was Article 371A added? → 1963 (13th Amendment)
☛ What does Article 371A protect? → Customary law and land ownership
☛ What is the purpose of special provisions for Nagaland? → Preservation of Naga culture and traditions
☛ Which state is related to Article 371G? → Mizoram
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से किस राज्य को अपनी अनूठी प्रथागत कानून और भूमि स्वामित्व प्रथाओं के कारण अनुच्छेद 371A के तहत विशेष प्रावधान प्राप्त हैं? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (29/08/2025) Shift 1)

मिजोरम
नागालैंड
मणिपुर
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है नागालैंड

Explanation:
अनुच्छेद 371A नागालैंड राज्य को विशेष प्रावधान प्रदान करता है। यह अनुच्छेद 1963 में जोड़ा गया था जब नागालैंड को एक राज्य का दर्जा दिया गया। इस अनुच्छेद का मुख्य उद्देश्य नागा लोगों की प्रथागत कानून, भूमि स्वामित्व और सामाजिक-धार्मिक प्रथाओं की रक्षा करना है। इसके तहत, संसद द्वारा बनाए गए कानून नागालैंड में तभी लागू होंगे जब राज्य का विधानमंडल उन्हें अपनाए। यह प्रावधान नागालैंड की अद्वितीय सांस्कृतिक पहचान और पारंपरिक शासन प्रणाली को संरक्षित रखता है। इसी प्रकार के विशेष प्रावधान अन्य उत्तर-पूर्वी राज्यों जैसे मिजोरम (अनुच्छेद 371G) और असम (अनुच्छेद 371B) के लिए भी हैं, लेकिन नागालैंड को अनुच्छेद 371A के तहत सबसे अधिक स्वायत्तता प्राप्त है।

question: Article 6 deals with persons who migrated to India from _____. (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (29/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Bangladesh
Sri Lanka
Pakistan
Nepal
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Pakistan

Explanation:
Article 6 of the Indian Constitution deals with persons who migrated to India from Pakistan after the partition. It grants citizenship to those who came from Pakistan before 26 January 1950 and have taken up permanent residence in India. This article was enacted to address the humanitarian crisis caused by the partition and to provide a legal framework for the citizenship of migrants. Article 6 is part of the citizenship provisions under Articles 5 to 11. It is distinct from Article 7, which deals with persons who migrated to Pakistan. The core intent of Article 6 is to ensure that those who migrated from Pakistan due to partition are considered Indian citizens if they fulfilled certain conditions.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ Which date is important for citizenship under Article 6? → 26 January 1950
☛ What does Article 7 deal with? → Persons who migrated to Pakistan
☛ What does Article 8 deal with? → Persons of Indian origin residing outside India
☛ Which articles of the Indian Constitution contain citizenship provisions? → Articles 5 to 11

question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution deals with Union Territories? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (29/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Article 7
Article 1
Article 262
Article 239
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 239

Explanation:
Article 239 of the Indian Constitution deals with the administration of Union Territories. According to this article, every Union Territory is administered by the President through an Administrator appointed by him. The President can appoint the executive head of a Union Territory as a Governor or Chief Commissioner. This article makes Union Territories centrally administered areas, where the central government has direct control. Article 239A allows the establishment of a legislature and council of ministers for certain Union Territories like Delhi and Puducherry. Article 240 empowers the President to make regulations for some Union Territories.

question: The Right to Protection in respect of conviction for offences (including protection from double jeopardy and self-incrimination) is covered under: (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (29/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Article 22
Article 20
Article 23
Article 21
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 20

Explanation:
Article 20 of the Indian Constitution provides protection in respect of conviction for offences. It includes three key safeguards: protection against ex post facto laws, double jeopardy, and self-incrimination. Ex post facto law means no person can be convicted for an act that was not an offence at the time of commission. Double jeopardy means no person can be prosecuted or punished for the same offence more than once. Protection against self-incrimination means no accused can be compelled to be a witness against themselves. Article 20 applies to both citizens and foreigners. It ensures fundamental fairness in criminal proceedings and upholds the rule of law.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ Article 20 applies to whom? → Both citizens and foreigners
☛ Article 20(1) deals with? → Ex post facto law
☛ Article 20(2) deals with? → Double jeopardy
☛ Article 20(3) deals with? → Self-incrimination

question: Which of the following subjects was NOT a part of the Transferred Subjects under the Government of India Act of 1919? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (29/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Local self-government
Police
Health
Education
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Police

Explanation:
The Government of India Act 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms) divided provincial subjects into two categories: Transferred and Reserved. Transferred subjects were controlled by Indian ministers responsible to the legislative council. These included education, health, local self-government, public works, and agriculture. In contrast, Reserved subjects remained under the governor and his executive council, including police, justice, finance, revenue, land revenue, and magisterial functions. Therefore, Police was not a transferred subject; it was a reserved subject. This was a key feature of dyarchy, ensuring that the British maintained control over law and order.

question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution empowers the Parliament and State Legislatures to make laws for the whole or any part of the territory of India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (29/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Article 250
Article 245
Article 249
Article 256
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 245

Explanation:
Article 245 of the Indian Constitution empowers the Parliament and State Legislatures to make laws for the whole or any part of India. Article 245(1) states that Parliament may make laws for the whole or any part of India, while Article 245(2) provides that State Legislatures may make laws for the whole or any part of their state. This article forms the basis of parliamentary supremacy and the federal structure. Article 250 grants Parliament the power to legislate on state subjects during a national emergency, Article 249 allows Parliament to legislate on state subjects in the national interest, and Article 256 directs states to comply with union laws.

question: Which of the following is a mode of losing Indian citizenship? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (29/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Renunciation
Birth
Registration
Naturalization
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Renunciation

Explanation:
According to the Citizenship Act, 1955, there are three modes of losing Indian citizenship: Renunciation, Termination, and Deprivation. Renunciation means a person voluntarily gives up their Indian citizenship. Birth, Registration, and Naturalization are modes of acquiring citizenship, not losing it. After renunciation, the person ceases to be an Indian citizen and loses certain rights.

question: Under what conditions can the Parliament legislate on matters in the State List according to constitutional provisions? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (29/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: When the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution.
During a national emergency declared under Article 352.
If the President signs a proclamation without Parliament's involvement.
If a Governor requests it due to a financial emergency in the state.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is When the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution.

Explanation:
Under Article 249 of the Constitution, if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution by a 2/3 majority of members present and voting that it is necessary in the national interest for Parliament to legislate on a matter in the State List, Parliament can do so. The resolution remains valid for a maximum of one year and can be renewed. During a national emergency under Article 352, Parliament can also legislate on State List subjects, but the question specifically refers to conditions under constitutional provisions, and Article 249 is the primary provision. Other options, like the President's proclamation or a Governor's request, are not constitutional provisions for such legislation. Thus, the correct condition is when the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution.

☛ Majority required for Rajya Sabha resolution → 2/3 of members present and voting.
☛ Maximum duration of resolution → One year, extendable.
☛ Article 352 → National emergency empowers Parliament to legislate on State List.
☛ Article 250 → Parliament's power to legislate on State List during emergency.

संविधान के अनुच्छेद 249 के अनुसार, यदि राज्यसभा 2/3 बहुमत से प्रस्ताव पारित करे कि राष्ट्रीय हित में संसद को राज्य सूची के किसी विषय पर कानून बनाना चाहिए, तो संसद ऐसा कर सकती है। यह प्रस्ताव अधिकतम एक वर्ष के लिए वैध होता है, जिसे बढ़ाया जा सकता है। अनुच्छेद 352 के तहत राष्ट्रीय आपातकाल के दौरान भी संसद राज्य सूची पर कानून बना सकती है, लेकिन यह विकल्प सही नहीं है क्योंकि प्रश्न में 'संवैधानिक प्रावधानों के अनुसार' का तात्पर्य अनुच्छेद 249 से है। अन्य विकल्प, जैसे राष्ट्रपति की घोषणा या राज्यपाल का अनुरोध, संवैधानिक प्रावधान नहीं हैं।

question: Lok Adalats in India have statutory status under which of the following enactments? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (29/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: The Civil Procedure Code, 1908
The Indian Penal Code, 1860
The Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987
The Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987

Explanation:
Lok Adalats in India have statutory status under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987. This Act was enacted to provide free legal aid to the poor and weaker sections of society. Lok Adalats are an important platform for alternative dispute resolution, where cases are resolved through mutual consent. Under this Act, the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) and State Legal Services Authorities were established. The decision of a Lok Adalat is final and binding on all parties, and no appeal lies against it.

question: Which of the following pairs of Union Territories were merged to form a single Indian Union Territory in 2020? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (29/08/2025) Shift 3)

question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution defined?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (29/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Article 6
Article 10
Article 11
Article 5
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 5

Explanation:
Article 5 of the Indian Constitution defines citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution. It grants citizenship to persons born in India, or either of whose parents was born in India, or who have been ordinarily resident in India for at least five years immediately before the commencement of the Constitution. Article 6 deals with citizenship of migrants from Pakistan, Article 10 ensures the continuance of citizenship rights, and Article 11 empowers Parliament to regulate citizenship by law. This article lays the foundation for citizenship provisions and is crucial for understanding the initial citizenship framework of India.

question: The Right to Constitutional Remedies, allowing individuals to move the Supreme Court directly for the enforcement of rights, is given under: (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (29/08/2025) Shift 3)

Article 30

question: Public Interest Litigation (PIL) in India is primarily associated with which of the following? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (29/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Police investigations
Judicial activism
Election Commission
Judicial review
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Judicial activism

Explanation:
Public Interest Litigation (PIL) in India is primarily associated with judicial activism, where the judiciary takes an active role in protecting social justice and the rights of marginalized groups. PIL originated in India in the 1980s, with the landmark case S.P. Gupta vs. Union of India (1981) laying its foundation. It allows any citizen to approach the court on matters of public interest, even if not directly affected. PIL is used for issues like environment, human rights, corruption, and governance. It differs from judicial review, which focuses on examining the constitutionality of laws, while PIL focuses on public interest issues. Police investigations and the Election Commission are not directly related to PIL. Judicial activism through PIL has expanded access to justice for the poor and disadvantaged.

question: Which Constitutional Amendment added the words 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (01/09/2025) Shift 1)
options: 42nd Amendment
38th Amendment
52nd Amendment
44th Amendment
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 42nd Amendment

Explanation:
The words 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity' were added to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act (1976). Enacted during the Indira Gandhi government, this amendment is often called the 'Mini Constitution' due to its extensive changes. 'Socialist' and 'Secular' were inserted between 'Sovereign' and 'Democratic Republic', while 'Integrity' was added after 'Unity of the Nation'. Besides the Preamble, the 42nd Amendment also added Fundamental Duties (Part IV-A) and altered the balance of power between the judiciary and the executive. It is one of the most significant amendments in Indian constitutional history, aimed at clarifying the ideological stance and strengthening the central government.

103वें संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 2019 द्वारा आर्थिक रूप से कमजोर वर्गों (EWS) को शैक्षणिक संस्थानों और सरकारी नौकरियों में 10% आरक्षण प्रदान किया गया। इस अधिनियम ने संविधान में अनुच्छेद 15(6) और अनुच्छेद 16(6) जोड़े। अनुच्छेद 15(6) राज्य को आर्थिक रूप से कमजोर वर्गों के लिए शैक्षणिक संस्थानों में प्रवेश में विशेष प्रावधान करने की अनुमति देता है, जबकि अनुच्छेद 16(6) सरकारी नौकरियों में उनके लिए आरक्षण का प्रावधान करता है। यह आरक्षण मौजूदा SC/ST/OBC आरक्षण के अतिरिक्त है और इसे 10 साल की अवधि के लिए लागू किया गया था। इस संशोधन ने आरक्षण के दायरे को आर्थिक मानदंडों पर आधारित किया, जो पहले केवल सामाजिक और शैक्षणिक पिछड़ेपन पर आधारित था।

question: Which of the following Directive Principles of State Policy is provided under Article 40 of the Indian Constitution?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (01/09/2025) Shift 2)

question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions the Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (01/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: Article 74
Article 80
Article 85
Article 76
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 74

Explanation:
Article 74 of the Indian Constitution provides for a Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President. It states that there shall be a Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister to assist the President in the exercise of his functions. The President is bound to act on the advice of the Council, and this became mandatory after the 42nd Amendment. Article 74 is fundamental to the parliamentary system, where the real executive power lies with the Council of Ministers. Article 75 deals with the appointment and responsibility of ministers. This ensures collective responsibility and democratic governance.
